text: Equal triangles which are on the same base, and on the same side, are also between the same parallels.  Let $ABC$ and $DBC$ be equal triangles which are on the same base $BC$, and on the same side (of it). I say that they are also between the same parallels.
I say that $AD$ and $BC$ are parallel.
assertion: what to show: AD and BC are parallel

text: For, if not, let $AE$ have been drawn through point A parallel to the straight-line $BC$ [Prop.~1.31],
Thus, triangle $ABC$ is equal to triangle $EBC$. For it is on the same base as it, $BC$, and between the same parallels [Prop.~1.37].

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: on the same base as it, $BC$, and between the same parallels

assertion: ABC is equal to DBC (the given)

text: Thus, $DBC$ is also equal to $EBC$, the greater to the lesser.
assertion: DBC is equal to EBC (greater to lesser)
AE is not parallel to BC

text: Similarly, we can show that neither (is) any other (straight-line) than $AD$.
assertion: no straight-line other than AD is parallel to BC

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: we can show that neither (is) any other (straight-line) than $AD$

text: Thus, equal triangles which are on the same base, and on the same side, are also between the same parallels. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
